title: The shifted resolution homology composite
statement: For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, an abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $X$, an injective resolution $I$ and $q\in\mathbf N$, write $R=f_*$ and $J=I[q]$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-raw-restricted-resolution-cocycle]. Define a sheaf morphism $T_{f,q,F,I}:H^0(RJ)\to H^q(R^+(F[0]))$ as follows. Apply $H^0$ to the canonical termwise shift map $R(I[q])\to R(I)[q]$, then apply the homology shift $H^0(R(I)[q])\to H^q(R(I))$, then the inverse of $I.\mathrm{isoRightDerivedObjCochainComplex}(R,q)$, then the inverse of $R.\mathrm{homologyRightDerivedFunctorPlusObjSingleFunctorIso}(F,q)$. Thus this morphism is the explicit four-factor composite of the prescribed maps, with its source expressed using the bounded-below shifted resolution. The notation and prescribed comparisons are those of [def-weil-pbc-raw-restricted-normalization-data] and [def-weil-pbc-abelian-higher-image-class].

proof.text: Use the existing direct-image commShift isomorphism and apply zeroth homology. Compose with the homology shift, the inverse classical resolution comparison, and the inverse comparison of classical right-derived functors with bounded-below derived homology. The shifted resolution has underlying complex I[q], so the first map has the declared source. The final comparison has the declared target. This directly constructs the map; there is no witness chosen from an unproved existence theorem. The same formula applies for q=0 and for the zero sheaf.
